newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Aug 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Aug 5.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Following strong prosecuting and video evidence, the Australian Football League Tribunal has issued a two-match suspension to Sydney players Tony Lockett, and a one match suspension to Sydney's Dale Lewis. Page 20.

Australian Rugby League chief executive Neil Whittaker is expected to present Super League executive director Ian Frykberg with a proposal incorporating major concessions which will make or break negotiations for a unified competition next year. Page 20.

Australian rugby union Wallaby captain John Eales has refuted claims that team morale was being undermined by the uncertain future of coach Greg Smith in the lead-up to the team's Tri-nations Test against the New Zealand All Blacks. Page 20.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Sydney Olympic chairman Gary Punch wants to accelerate the privatisation plans of the Australian soccer club, which is currently managed by a private consortium and which carries a long-standing debt of around $600,000. Page 45.

New South Wales Rugby League judiciary chairman Alan Sullivan has warned South Sydney player Darrell Trindall his career is at risk if he continues with his controversial tackling style. The warning was given after Sullivan issued Trindall with a six match suspension for a careless high tackle. Page 45.

Australian equestrian rider Andrew Hoy beat three-time winner Mary King in drizzling rain to take gold in the British Open at Captain Mark Phillips' Gatcombe Park facility on Sunday. Hoy is now the first Australian to achieve that honour. Page 45.
THE AGE

The Australian Football League has announced it will look into a behind-the-play incident during last Sunday's Adelaide-Carlton game in which Carlton utility Trent Ormond-Allen suffered a broken jaw. Ormond-Allen is expected to be out of the game for at last six weeks. Page B8.
Australian runner Darren Wilson has qualified for the finals of the 10,000 metres at the world track and field championships in Athens. Wilson finished fifth in 27 minutes and 57.54 seconds. Page B6.

Australian Football League St Kilda's half-forward, Joel Smith, is expected to be side-lined for the next 12 months following the first of two knee operations to repair his severely damaged medial and posterior cruciate ligaments. Page B8.
THE HERALD SUN

Australian Football League team Collingwood has lost defender Scott Burns for the remainder of the season. Burns aggravated a chronic groin injury during a match against St Kilda last Sunday at the Melbourne Cricket Grounds and is expected to consult a surgeon. Page 69.

Australian golfer Stuart Appleby regained his spot on the top ten earners list when he finished runner-up at the $2.3 million Sprint International tournament. Appleby's performance continues a dream season for him on the US Tour with less than two weeks of the US PGA championships. Page 68.

Victory in yesterday's Brazilian Grand Prix has placed Australian Michael Doohan 10 points away from winning a fourth consecutive 500cc motorcycle world championship title. Doohan is 116 points ahead of his Japanese team-mate Tadayuki Okada. Page 68.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH
Australia has retained the top spot in track cycling after clinching medals in all but one contested race, including four gold, at the world junior championships in South Africa. Page 62.

Australian Football League Adelaide Crow's coach Malcolm Blight said his team has the second best defensive record in the competition behind Sydney, in addition to the best attack record in league. Page 61.

Australian Rugby League captains yesterday campaigned for the introduction of the in-goal video replay system during the upcoming finals series in a move which follows the policy adopted by Super League. Page 60.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
